'''Regina Catholic Education Center''' is a PK–12 [[Private school|private]], [[Catholic Church|Roman Catholic]] [[Mixed-sex education|co-educational]] school in [[Iowa City, Iowa|Iowa City]], [[Iowa]], United States. It is located in the [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Davenport]].

== Athletics ==
Regina's sports teams are known as the '''Regals''', with a school mascot named "Crownie," an anthropomorphic blue and gold crown.

The Regals won a state football championship in 2005, and more recently have won a state record six titles in a row from 2010 to 2015,<ref>K. J. Pilcher, [http://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/regals-claim-sixth-straight-state-crown-20151123 "Regals claim sixth straight state crown"], ''[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]]'', November 23, 2015.</ref> a string that included a record 56 game winning streak from 2010 to 2013.<ref>Ryan Murken, [http://www.press-citizen.com/story/sports/high-school/football/2015/11/22/coaching-staff-boost-regina/76229532/ "Coaching staff a boost for Regina"], ''[[Iowa City Press-Citizen]]'', November 22, 2015.</ref>  From 2007 to 2020, the team was coached by former NFL tight end [[Marv Cook]], who attended high school at Regina's conference rival [[West Branch, Iowa|West Branch]] High School.<ref>Rob Poggenklass, [http://www.westbranchtimes.com/article.php?id=1557 "Marv Cook named head coach at Regina"], ''West Branch Times'', March 7, 2007.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021 |title=Marv Cook steps down as Regina football coach |url=https://www.thegazette.com/iowa-prep-sports/marv-cook-steps-down-as-regina-football-coach/ |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=The Gazette |language=en-US}}</ref>

The Regals have won eight state titles in boys' cross-country since 1993.<ref>[http://www.iahsaa.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/10/2013_CrossCountry_StatBook2.pdf ''2013 IHSAA Cross Country State Meet History and Stat Book''], p. 13.</ref>  The girls' softball team took the state title in 2011.<ref>Jeff Lindor, [http://www.kcrg.com/sports/local/A-Crown-for-the-Regals-in-2A-Softball-126048743.html "A Crown for the Regals in 2A Softball"], [[KCRG-TV]], July 22, 2011.</ref>

=== State championships ===
* Boys' Cross Country - 8-time State Champions (1993, 1997, 1998, 2003, 2004, 2006, 2007, 2010, 2022)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iahsaa.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/2020-XC-Stat-Book-12.16.19.pdf|title=2020 IHSAA Cross Country Stat Book|publisher=[[Iowa High School Athletic Association]]|date=2019-12-16|access-date=2020-07-23}}</ref>
* Boys' Soccer - 8-time Class 1A State Champions (2009, 2010, 2011, 2013, 2014, 2017, 2018, 2019)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iahsaa.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/SoccerStatbook.pdf|title=2020 Soccer Stat Book|publisher=[[Iowa High School Athletic Association]]|date=2019-06-12|access-date=2020-09-20}}</ref>
* Football - 8-time State Champions (2005, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2020)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iahsaa.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/2024-Football-RB-7.3.24.pdf|title=IHSAA 2023 Football Record Book|publisher=[[Iowa High School Athletic Association]]|date=April 5, 2024|access-date=July 7, 2024}}</ref>
* Boys' Basketball -3 time Class 1A State Champions (1976, 1978, 1979)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iahsaa.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2020-Basketball-Stat-Book-1.29.20.pdf|title=2020 State Tournament Stat Book Basketball|publisher=[[Iowa High School Athletic Association]]|date=2020-01-29|access-date=2020-07-23}}</ref>
* Softball - 4-time Class 2A State Champions (2011, 2015, 2017, 2023)<ref>{{cite web|title=State Softball Record Book |url=https://ighsau.org/upl/downloads/library/state-softball-record-book-7-9-18.pdf |publisher=Iowa Girls High School Athletic Union |date=9 July 2018 |accessdate=13 September 2021}}</ref>
* Girls' Golf - 2009 Class 2A State Champions<ref>{{cite web| url=https://sites.google.com/site/iahsaasports/iowa-high-schools/current-high-schools/regina |title=Regina |publisher=Iowa High School Sports |access-date=November 28, 2021}}</ref>
* Girls' Track and Field - 1995 Class 1A State Champions<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ighsau.org/upl/downloads/library/track-2019-recordbook6-18-19.pdf|title=2019 IGHSAU Track & Field Record Book|publisher=[[Iowa Girls High School Athletic Union]]|date=2019-05-13|access-date=2020-08-23}}</ref>
